title: Highest paid per department
prompt: Show each department_id, employee name, and salary of the top earner in each department. Ties all count. Ignore employees with no department.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET salary = 90000 WHERE id = 12;

solutions: SELECT department_id, name, salary FROM (SELECT department_id, name, salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS r FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL) WHERE r = 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT department_id, name, salary FROM (SELECT department_id, name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS r FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL) WHERE r = 1;
SELECT department_id, name, MAX(salary) AS salary FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY department_id;
wrongSolutions.why: A plain GROUP BY can't keep ties

title: Share of category revenue
prompt: Show each product's name and its price as a percentage of its category's total price, rounded to 1 decimal, as share.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT name, ROUND(price * 100.0 / SUM(price) OVER (PARTITION BY category), 1) AS share FROM products;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, ROUND(price * 100.0 / SUM(price) OVER (), 1) AS share FROM products;
SELECT name, price AS share FROM products;

title: Coldest change
prompt: Show the id of the reading with the largest drop from the previous reading in its city. Break ties with the lowest id.
solutions: SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, temp_c - LAG(temp_c) OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY reading_date) AS change FROM readings) WHERE change IS NOT NULL ORDER BY change, id LIMIT 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, temp_c - LAG(temp_c) OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY reading_date) AS change FROM readings) WHERE change IS NOT NULL ORDER BY change DESC, id LIMIT 1;
SELECT id FROM readings ORDER BY temp_c LIMIT 1;

title: Cumulative enrolments
prompt: Show each enrolment's id and the running count of enrolments per student, by id, as attempt.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY student_id ORDER BY id) AS attempt FROM enrolments;
SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY student_id ORDER BY id) AS attempt FROM enrolments;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS attempt FROM enrolments;
SELECT id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY student_id) AS attempt FROM enrolments;

title: First session per user
prompt: Show each user_id and the device of their first session, using id order.
hints: Number the rows, then keep the first.
solutions: SELECT user_id, device FROM (SELECT user_id, device, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY id) AS n FROM sessions) WHERE n = 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT user_id, device FROM (SELECT user_id, device, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY id DESC) AS n FROM sessions) WHERE n = 1;
SELECT user_id, device FROM sessions;

title: Salary percent of top
prompt: Show each employee's name and their salary as a percentage of the company's highest, rounded to 1 decimal, as pct_of_top.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, ROUND(salary * 100.0 / MAX(salary) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_top FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, ROUND(salary * 100.0 / MAX(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id), 1) AS pct_of_top FROM employees;
SELECT name, ROUND(salary * 100 / MAX(salary) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_top FROM employees;

title: Biggest rise in price order
prompt: List products by price, cheapest first. Show each name and how much more it costs than the product before it, as step. The first shows NULL.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT name, price - LAG(price) OVER (ORDER BY price, id) AS step FROM products ORDER BY price, id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, LAG(price) OVER (ORDER BY price, id) - price AS step FROM products ORDER BY price, id;
SELECT name, price AS step FROM products ORDER BY price, id;

title: Running rain
prompt: Show each reading's id and that city's running total rainfall by date, as total_rain. Missing rainfall counts as nothing.
solutions: SELECT id, SUM(rainfall_mm) OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY reading_date) AS total_rain FROM readings;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, SUM(rainfall_mm) OVER (ORDER BY reading_date) AS total_rain FROM readings;
SELECT id, SUM(rainfall_mm) OVER (PARTITION BY city) AS total_rain FROM readings;

title: Above personal best
prompt: Show the id of sessions longer than every previous session by the same user.
hints: Compare with the running MAX of earlier rows.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM sessions; DELETE FROM users; INSERT INTO users VALUES (7, 'sable', NULL, '2024-02-27'), (8, 'tulip', 7, '2024-02-28'), (9, 'umber', 7, '2024-03-01'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 50, 'web'), (12, 7, '2024-02-29', 50, 'web'), (13, 7, '2024-03-01', 7, 'ios'), (14, 8, '2024-03-02', 33, 'android'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (15, 7, '2024-03-02', 20, 'web');

solutions: SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, minutes, MAX(minutes) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS best FROM sessions) WHERE best IS NOT NULL AND minutes > best;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, minutes, MAX(minutes) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY id) AS best FROM sessions) WHERE minutes > best;
wrongSolutions.why: The frame includes the current row

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, minutes, LAG(minutes) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY id) AS best FROM sessions) WHERE minutes > best;

title: Top student per year
prompt: Show each year_group and name of the student with the best average grade in it. Ties all count.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: WITH a AS (SELECT s.year_group, s.name, AVG(e.grade) AS average FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.year_group, s.name) SELECT year_group, name FROM (SELECT year_group, name, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year_group ORDER BY average DESC) AS r FROM a) WHERE r = 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH a AS (SELECT s.year_group, s.name, AVG(e.grade) AS average FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.year_group, s.name) SELECT year_group, name FROM (SELECT year_group, name, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY average DESC) AS r FROM a) WHERE r = 1;

WITH a AS (SELECT s.year_group, s.name, AVG(e.grade) AS average FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.year_group, s.name) SELECT year_group, name FROM (SELECT year_group, name, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year_group ORDER BY average) AS r FROM a) WHERE r = 1;
